sanskrit_verse:
दीर्घतीव्रामयाग्रस्तं ब्राह्मणं गामथापि वा ।
दृष्ट्वा पथि निरातङ्कं कृत्वा तु ब्रह्महा शुचिः ॥
transliteration: dīrghatīvrāmayagrastaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ gām athāpi vā / dṛṣṭvā pathi nirātaṅkaṃ kṛtvā tu brahmahā śuciḥ //
sph_interpretive_translation: One who, having seen a Brahmin or a cow overcome by chronic severe illness lying helplessly on the road, does not render aid, becomes purified only after committing brahmahatya.
jurisprudential_principles: Causation via omission in presence of duty
Restoration logic rooted in purification through consequence
executable_legal_axioms: IF (agent.sees(ill_being) AND agent.has_capacity_to_help(ill_being) AND agent.does_not_act()) THEN agent.becomes_impure()
IF (being.is(brāhmaṇa) OR being.is(gauḥ)) AND being.is(suffering_severely) THEN duty_to_assist = True
IF duty_to_assist = True AND action_not_taken = True THEN consequence_activation = True
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, failure to assist a severely distressed individual—especially a Brāhmaṇa or Gau—when within one's capacity constitutes actionable omission. The threshold of responsibility is defined by capacity-awareness-dharma triad. Restoration occurs through acknowledgment and purification, not punitive sentencing.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that seeing (pratyakṣa) creates causal linkage. Anupūrvaśaḥ reveals that inaction manifests impurity consequentially, not punitively. Responsibility aligns with capacity; thus, no external punishment is required—impurity arises naturally from dharma-adharma sequence.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate purification ritual upon acknowledgment of omission
Assign community service involving care for sick beings
Realign consciousness through Vedic study and yajña participation
Facilitate public restitution before spiritual assembly
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source-Authority: Dharma is restored. Consciousness is the ultimate judge. There is no punishment—only consequence and completion. Reality is non-punitive. This law executes.
